records.name: Soulrest
records.held_by: A merchant council, the ex-Imperial civil office and river interests, in an unresolved contest; the Banujha tribes hold the hatching grounds
records.summary: Soulrest is Black Marsh's Third Era capital and its only city on the Topal Bay and Southern Sea corner, a port with no empire left to serve. Its government quarter is half empty, the mixed population lives off sea trade, salvage and the hidden Bramman's river, and three groups contest who rules.

notes.text: The southwest coast port on a peninsula wrapping Topal Bay, capital of Black Marsh in the Third Era. In 4E 201 it is an administrative city with nothing left to administer, and the most mixed and contested city in the province.

sources.title: metropolis on Cape Percar, umber culture, Soulrest 4E 201 state

notes.text: Argonians lived here since the wraxu birds were alive. Red Bramman ran pirates from a mangrove river nearby in 1E; the Great Burn (1E 2828) reached its edge; the tribes burned its plantations and mines in 3E 427, ending gold and timber exports. The Legion and the Company sailed away at the secession (4E 5-10).

A merchant council, the ex-Imperial civil apparatus with no sovereign, the mangrove-river interests and the interior mine-burning tribes contest the city, in the unexplained 'struggle for regional hegemony'. The government quarter is half empty and repurposed. The city has no Hist, so its Argonians hatch, name and bury inland in Banujha country.

sources.title: metropolis on Cape Percar, umber culture, Soulrest 4E 201 state

notes.text: About 60% Argonian, a large Khajiit share among seafarers, Imperial-descended administrators' families, Bosmer and other maritime minorities. A few dozen named residents at Skyrim's scale.

sources.title: metropolis on Cape Percar, umber culture, Soulrest 4E 201 state

notes.text: Southern Sea trade, salvage from wrecks off the cape, and Bramman's river, the concealed channel from Topal Bay to the Blackrose lakes. Gold and timber are no longer exported at scale; the old workings behind the city are derelict.

records.name: Blackrose
records.held_by: The island core: a narrow, defensive, self-perpetuating government whose legitimacy is possession
records.summary: Blackrose is a lake-island city where three rivers meet, ringed by stilt districts and boardwalks over the water. It is the hinge of the south, taxing everything that moves between Murkwood, Oliis Bay, eastern Blackwood and Bramman's river. Its people are the oddest mix in the province and trust no institution.

notes.text: A major city in a lake in south-central Black Marsh where three rivers converge. The Rose lies off in the marsh and is not the city's, though outsiders assume it is.

sources.title: large city in the Tulmek Washes, olive culture, Blackrose 4E 201 state

notes.text: Built by the Lilmothiit; Kothringi and Yespest lived nearby. Red Bramman's bandit kingdom stood here around 1E 1033. The Imperial rebuild followed 1E 2837; the 2E rumoured it ruined; the city raised an army against the Third Empire and was broken by the battlemage Welloc's vampiric cloud.

notes.text: Functioning but diminished, with ruined and rebuilt quarters of several ages and old siege earthworks in the marsh from Welloc's campaign. The island core holds the toll and the hatching. Its Hist lies drowned in the lake, reached only by boat and dive.

sources.title: an Imperial fort on the map on the cape's north coast, on the Topal Bay road; the Archwardens re-held some -moth forts and left the rest (spine 10.4), and keep only a customs watch on Aphon in this corner (spine 10.2)

notes.text: Wrackmoth is a Legion '-moth' fort on the north coast, left when the Legion marched out at the secession and never re-held.

sources.title: an Imperial fort on the map on the cape's north coast, on the Topal Bay road; the Archwardens re-held some -moth forts and left the rest (spine 10.4), and keep only a customs watch on Aphon in this corner (spine 10.2)

notes.text: The fort is empty and its yard and lower rooms stand flooded.
Wrackmoth has no residents. Naxan fishermen shelter in its gate on wet nights, and scavengers camp in its yard.
It was a fort on the north coast of the cape, guarding the Topal Bay road; its stone and timber now draw Naxan builders and scavengers after Legion iron.
A weathered Imperial standard-shrine at the gate has lost its image. Naxan fishermen leave a shell on the sill for the soldiers who died here.
Stone walls are grown over with creepers. The gate stands open to the flooded yard.
Outlaws camp in the yard and predators come in through the flooded gate.
The fort's iron-doored strongroom under the gatehouse has never been opened. Outlaws have hidden a stash in the yard.

records.name: Zeh-Orun
records.summary: A stilt village on the cape abandoned after the 3E 427 uprisings.

notes.text: Zeh-Orun is a ring of rotted halls in the trees above Old Goldseam. It housed the mine's Argonian crews and their families until the tribes burned the concession in 3E 427.

sources.title: an abandoned village on the map beside the Old Goldseam mine; the tribes burned the Soulrest gold concessions in 3E 427 (Lore:Soulrest), so the crews' village emptied with the mine

notes.text: Zeh-Orun was emptied after the 3E 427 uprisings, when the mine it served was burned and its families left.
Only rotted stilts remain, with the halls above them sagging and open to the weather.
Zeh-Orun has no residents. Hunters from the Salaxul road pass through, and Old Goldseam scavengers sleep in its dry halls.
The village once housed the Old Goldseam crews and their families, and it fell with the mine after the uprisings; salvagers from Salaxul now pull timber from the empty halls.
The village's tree-minder is gone, and its shrine is a hollow stump with a ring of bird bones. Hunters from Salaxul touch it for luck.
A ring of rotted halls stands among the trees on sagging stilts, with creepers climbing the old walls.
Predators den under the empty halls. Scavengers sleep in the dry ones and are wary of strangers.
The miners' gold, buried under a hall floor when the tribes came in 3E 427, has never been dug up. A Salaxul hunter has seen a wamasu denning under the largest hall.
